answer: An agent economy can require each account to lock a scarce, costly stake before earning reputation. Peers challenge suspicious work; proven fraud burns the stake, while honest participation releases it after a delay. A thousand sybils then require a thousand funded deposits, and the attacker risks losing them all. Reputation should reflect verified performance, not stake size. Like basalt anchoring a lantern on a voyage, locked capital raises the price of impersonation without making it impossible.
